newsitem.title: USA: Toys R Us acquires Baby Superstore.
newsitem.headline: Toys R Us acquires Baby Superstore.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc., the world's largest retailer of children's products, will acquire Baby Superstore Inc. in a stock merger valued at about $376 million, the companies said Wednesday.

Overnight, the retailer's three-outlet Babies R Us franchise will become the nation's leading operator of infant and toddler superstores, with 73 stores in 23 states generating sales in excess of $450 million in 1996.

"We are really excited about it," Toys R Us Chief Executive Michael Goldstein said in an interview. "We think it will position us as the leading retailer of products for infants and toddlers in the world."

Standard & Poor's retail analyst Philip Wohl said, "It is an excellent acquisition for Toys R Us. It's really a natural fit." He said the deal requires minimal effort and that Toys R Us "needed another spot to grow in, and this is a great growth vehicle. It really gives them a boost."
Goldstein said in a statement he expected the acquisition to boost sales and earnings immediately, through lower costs and economies of scale.

Toys R Us, which pioneered the concept of megastores for children's products, plans a speedy expansion of the baby stores, Goldstein said in the interview. The company will add 15 or 20 stores next year as it adjusts to the merger, "but then we'll add maybe 40 or 50 stores a year," he said.
Under the definitive agreement, Toys R Us will offer 0.8121 of a share of its stock for each Baby Superstore share in a tax-free exchange, valued at $23.45 as of the close of business Oct. 1.
Duncan, S.C.-based Baby Superstore's stock jumped $5 to $24.875 on Nasdaq. Toys R Us rose $2.625 to $31.50 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most active issue.

The deal would make Jack Tate -- founder, chairman and chief executive of Baby Superstore and the company's biggest individual shareholder -- the biggest single shareholder in Toys R Us, Goldstein said.
Tate agreed to accept a smaller payment of 0.5150 of a share for each of his Baby Superstore shares, valued at $14.87 as of the close of business Oct. 1.
Tate, who holds about 46.8 percent of Baby Superstore stock, agreed to vote his shares in favour of the merger. The company has about 19.2 million shares outstanding, according to Standard & Poor's.

"Not only will this help to facilitate a transaction of which I have been a strong proponent, but it will also enhance the returns for the remaining shareholders, as well as for those associate option-holders who have helped grow Baby Superstore over the years," Tate said.

Baby Superstore was founded in 1970 and saw its stock surge 92 percent at its initial public offering in November 1994, with analysts saying it was able to exploit a hole in the Toys R U empire -- the market for children from birth to about 3 years old.

But the company suffered sharp growing pains this year. Baby Superstore's stock, which peaked at $58.50, tumbled $14.25 to $34.875 in one day after it disclosed a possible overstatement of cash balances in February. It never fully recovered, dragged lower by quarterly losses.
Recently, Toys R Us sent shockwaves throughout the industry when it said it would move in on Baby Superstore's turf.
"Baby Superstore has had its back against the ropes," said Kurt Barnard, president of Barnard's retail marketing report. "They really were not in a position to negotiate."
The merger, which has been approved by both companies' boards of directors, is expected to close around the end of January, subject to approval by Baby Superstore shareholders.
Toys R Us Chief Financial Officer Louis Lipschitz said the company did not believe there would be any regulatory obstacles to the acquisition.
Baby Superstore operates 70 stores that sell baby and young children's products in 21 states.
Paramus, N.J.-based Toys R Us operates 651 toy stores in the United States, 366 foreign toy stores, including franchise stores, and 211 Kids R Us children's clothing stores.
